transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think the principal that separates me is that 5 and a half million people came together on their own and put me on the ballot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I was not put on the ballot by either of the 2 parties; I was not put on the ballot by any PAC money, by any foreign lobbyist money, by any special interest money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This is a movement that came from the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This is the way the framers of the Constitution intended our government to be, a government that comes from the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Over time we have developed a government that comes at the people, that comes from the top down, where the people are more or less treated as objects to be programmed during the campaign with commercials and media events and fear messages and personal attacks and things of that nature.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The thing that separates my candidacy and makes it unique is that this came from millions of people in 50 states all over this country who wanted a candidate that worked and belonged to nobody but them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I go into this race as their servant, and I belong to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So this comes from the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The most important distinction in this campaign is that I represent real hope for change, a departure from trickle-down economics, a departure from tax and spend economics, to invest in growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But before I can do that, I must challenge the American people to change, and they must decide.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Tonight I say to the President: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush, for 12 years you’ve had it your way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You’ve had your chance and it didn’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s time to change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to bring that change to the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we must all decide first we have the courage to change for hope and a better tomorrow.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think one thing that distinguishes is experience.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we’ve dramatically changed the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll talk about that a little bit later, but the changes are mind-boggling for world peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Kids go to bed at night without the same fear of nuclear war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And change for change sake isn’t enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We saw that message in the late 70s when heard a lot about change, and what happened, that misery index went right through the roof.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But my economic program is the kind of change we want.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the way we’re going to get it done is we’re going to have a brand new Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A lot of them are thrown out because of all the scandals.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll sit down with them, Democrats and Republicans alike, and work for my agenda for American renewal, which represents real change.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I’d say, if you had to separate out, I think it’s experience at this level.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I believe experience counts, but it’s not everything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Values, judgment, and the record that I have amassed in my state also should count for something.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve worked hard to create good jobs and to educate people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My state now ranks first in the country in job growth this year, fourth in income growth, fourth in reduction of poverty, third in overall economic performance, according to a major news magazine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s because we believe in investing in education and in jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we have to change in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, my wife, Hillary, gave me a book about a year ago in which the author defined insanity as just doing the same old thing over and over again and expecting a different result.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have got to have the courage to change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Experience is important, yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve gotten a lot of good experience in dealing with ordinary people over the last year and month.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve touched more people’s lives and seen more heartbreak and hope, more pain and more promise, than anybody else who’s run for president this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think the American people deserve better than they’re getting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have gone from first to thirteenth in wages in the world in the last twelve years, since Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush and Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Reagan have been in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Personal income has dropped while people have worked harder.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In the last four years, there have been twice as many bankruptcies as new jobs created.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need a new approach.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The same old experience is not relevant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re living in a new world after the Cold War, and what works in this new world is not trickle down, not government for the benefit of the privileged few, not tax and spend, but a commitment to invest in American jobs and American education, controlling American health care costs, and bringing the American people together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is what works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you can have the right kind of experience and the wrong kind of experience.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mine is rooted in the real lives of real people, and it will bring real results if we have the courage to change.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just thought of another — another big difference here between me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Perot feels this way, but I know Governor Clinton did because I want to accurately quote him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He thinks, I think he said, that the country is coming apart at the seams.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, I know that the only way he can win is to make everybody believe the economy’s worse than it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But this country is not coming apart at the seams, for heaven’s sakes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In spite of the economic problems, we’re the most respected economy around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Many would trade for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve been caught up in a global slowdown.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can do much, much better, but we ought not try to convince the American people that America is a country that’s coming apart at the seams.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would hate to be running for president and think that the only way I could win would be to convince everybody how horrible things are.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, there are big problems, and yes, people are hurting.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I believe that this Agenda for American renewal I have is the answer to do it, and I believe we can get it done now, whereas we didn’t in the past, because you’re going to have a whole brand new bunch of people in the Congress that are going to have to listen to the same American people I’m listening to.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, they’ve got a point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have any experience in running up a $4 trillion debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have any experience in gridlock government where nobody takes responsibility for anything and everybody blames everybody else.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have any experience in creating the worst public school system in the industrialized world, the most violent crime-ridden society in the industrialized world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Â But I do have a lot of experience in getting things done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So, if we’re at a point in history where we want to stop talking about it and do it, I’ve got a lot of experience in figuring out how to solve problems, making the solutions work, and then moving on to the next one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got a lot of experience in not taking 10 years to solve a 10-minute problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So, if it’s time for action, I think I have experience that counts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If there’s more time for gridlock and talk and finger pointing, I’m the wrong man.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the American people should be the judge of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think character is a very important question.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I said something the other day where I was accused of being like Joe McCarthy because I questioned — I put it this way; I think it’s wrong to demonstrate against your own country or organize demonstrations against your own country in foreign soil.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just think it’s wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I — well, maybe they say, “Well, it was a youthful indiscretion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” I was 19 or 20 flying off an aircraft carrier and that shaped me to be Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m sorry, but demonstrating — it’s not a question of patriotism.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a question of character and judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They get on me — Bill’s gotten on me about, “read my lips.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” When I make a mistake I’ll admit it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But he has made — not admitted a mistake and I just find it impossible to understand how an American can demonstrate against his own country in a foreign land — organizing demonstrations against it when young men are held prisoner in Hanoi or kids out of the ghetto were drafted.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Some say, “well, you’re a little old fashioned.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” Maybe I am, but I just don’t think that’s right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, whether it’s character or judgment — whatever it is — I have a big difference here on this issue and so we’ll just have to see how it plays out.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I — I couldn’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t think most Americans could do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And they all say, “Well, it was a long time ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” Well, let’s admit it then.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Say, “I made a terrible mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” How could you be Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces and have some kid say — when you have to make a tough decision, as I did in Panama or Kuwait and then have some kid jump up and say, “Well, I’m not going to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Commander-in-Chief was organizing demonstrations halfway around the world during another era.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So there are differences but that’s about the main area where I think we have a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know about — we’ll talk about that a little with Ross here in a bit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think the American people will make their own decisions on character and at a time when we have work to do and we need action I think they need to clearly understand the backgrounds of each person.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think the press can play a huge roll in making sure that the backgrounds are clearly presented in an objective way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then, make a decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Certainly anyone in the White House should have the character to be there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But, I think it’s very important to measure when and where things occurred.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Did they occur when you were a young person, in your formative years?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Or did they occur while you were a senior official in the federal government?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: When youâ€™re a senior official in the federal government spending billions of dollars in taxpayerâ€™s money and youâ€™re a mature individual and you make a mistake, then that was on our ticket.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you make it as a young man, time passes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So I would say just, you know, look at all three of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Decide who you think will do the job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Pick that person in November because believe me, as I’ve said before, “The party’s over and it’s time for the clean-up crew.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: ” And we do have to have change and people who never take responsibility for anything when it happens on their watch and people who are in charge —

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The time is up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: More later.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Ross gave a good answer but I’ve got to respond directly to Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You have questioned my patriotism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You even brought some right-wing congressman into the White House to plot how to attack me for going to Russia in 1969-70, when over 50,000 other Americans did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, I honor your service in World War II, I honor Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot’s service in uniform and the service of every man and woman who ever served, including Admiral Crowe, who was your Chairman of the joint Chiefs and who’s supporting me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But when Joe McCarthy went around this country attacking people’s patriotism he was wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He was wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And a senator from Connecticut stood up to him named Prescott Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Your father was right to stand up to Joe McCarthy, you were wrong to attack my patriotism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I was opposed to the war but I loved my country and we need a president who will bring this country together, not divide it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had enough division.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to lead a unified country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The tax increase I have proposed triggers in at family incomes of $200,000 and above.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Those are the people who in the 1980s had their incomes go up while their taxes went down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Middle-class people, defined as people with incomes of $52,000 and down, had their incomes go down while their taxes went up in the Reagan-Bush years because of 6 increases in the payroll taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So that is where my income limit would trigger.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My plan –

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: –notwithstanding my opponent’s ad, my plan triggers in at gross incomes, family incomes of $200,000 and above.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Then we want to give modest middle-class tax relief to restore some fairness, especially to middle- class people with families with incomes of under $60,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In addition to that, the money that I raise from upper-income people and from asking foreign corporations just to pay the same income on their income earned in America that American corporations do will be used to give incentives back to upper-income people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to give people permanent incentives on investment tax credit, like President Kennedy and the Congress inaugurated in the early ’60s to get industry moving again; a research and development tax credit; a low-income housing tax credit; a long-term capital gains proposal for new business and business expansions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to have no more trickle down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We don’t need across-the-board tax cuts for the wealthy for nothing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to say here’s your tax incentive: if you create American jobs, the old-fashioned way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to create more millionaires than were created under Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush and Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Reagan, but I don’t want to have 4 years where we have no growth in the private sector, and that’s what’s happened in the last 4 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re down 35,000 jobs in the private sector.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to invest and grow, and that’s what I want to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me–I have to correct one thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t question the man’s patriotism.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I questioned his judgment and his character.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What he did in Moscow, that’s fine.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let him explain it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He did.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I accept that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What I don’t accept is demonstrating and organizing demonstrations in a foreign country when your country’s at war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I cannot accept that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In terms of this one on taxes spells out the biggest difference between us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do not believe we need to go back to the Mondale proposals or the Dukakis proposals of tax and spend.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Governor Clinton says $200,000 but he also says he wants to raise $150 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Taxing people over $200,000 will not get you $150 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then when you add in his other spending proposals, regrettably you end up socking it to the working man.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That old adage they use–we’re going to soak the rich- -we’re going to soak the rich–it always ends up being the poor cab driver or the working man that ends up paying the bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I just have a different approach.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe the way to get the deficit down is to control the growth of mandatory spending programs, and not raise taxes on the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a big difference there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to have a growing, expanding job base to give us a growing, expanding tax base.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Right now we have a flat to deteriorating job base and where it appears to be growing, it’s minimum-wage jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve got to really rebuild our job base.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s going to take money for infrastructure and investment to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Our foreign competitors are doing it; we’re not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We cannot pay off the $4 trillion debt, balance the budget and have the industries of the future and the high- paying jobs in this country without having the revenue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to go through a period of shared sacrifice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: There’s one challenge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s got to be fair.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve created a mess, don’t have much to show for it and we have got to fix it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And that’s about all I can say in a minute.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, Sander, that’s a good question, and the answer is: for 40-some years we kept the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you look at the cost of not keeping the peace in Europe, it would be exorbitant.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have reduced the number of troops that are deployed and going to be deployed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have cut defense spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the reason we could do that is because of our fantastic success in winning the Cold War.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We never would have got there if we had gone for the nuclear freeze crowd; we never would have got there if we had listened to those that wanted to cut defense spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it is important that the US stay in Europe and continue to guarantee the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We simply cannot pull back.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, when anybody has a spending program they want to spend money on at home, they say, well, let’s cut money out of the Defense Dept.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I will accept and have accepted the recommendations of 2 proven leaders, General Colin Powell and Secretary Dick Cheney.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They feel that the levels we’re operating at and the reductions that I have proposed are proper.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I simply do not think we should go back to the isolation days and starting blaming foreigners.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We are the sole remaining superpower, and we should be that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we have a certain disproportionate responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I would ask the American people to understand that if we make imprudent cuts, if we go too far, we risk the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t want to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve seen what it is like to see a war, to see the burdens of a war, and I don’t want to see us make reckless cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because of our programs we have been able to significantly cut defense spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But let’s not cut into the muscle, and let’s not cut down our insurance policy, which is participation of American forces in NATO, the greatest peace- keeping organization ever made.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Today you’ve got problems in Europe, still bubbling along even though Europe’s gone democracy’s route.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we are there, and I think this insurance policy is necessary.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it goes with world leadership, and I think the levels we’ve come up with are just about right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If I’m poor and you’re rich, and I can get you to defend me, that’s good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But when the tables get turned, I ought to do my share.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Right now we spend about $300 billion a year on defense, the Japanese spend around 30 billion in Asia, the Germans spend around 30 billion in Europe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: For example, Germany will spend a trillion dollars building infrastructure over the next 10 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s kind of easy to do if you only have to pick up a $30-billion tab to defend your country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The European Community is in a position to pay a lot more than they have in the past.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I agree with the president: when they couldn’t, we should have; now that they can, they should.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We sort of seem to have a desire to try to stay over there and control it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They don’t want us to control it, very candidly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So it I think is very important for us to let them assume more and more of the burden and for us to bring that money back here and rebuild our infrastructure, because we can only be a superpower if we are an economic superpower; and we can only be an economic superpower if we have a growing, expanding job base.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I agree with the general statement Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush made.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I disagree that we need 150,000 troops to fulfill our role in Europe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We certainly must maintain an engagement there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are certainly dangers there, there are certainly other trouble spots in the world which are closer to Europe than to the US.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But 2 former defense secretaries recently issued a report saying that 100,000 or slightly fewer troops would be enough, including President Reagan’s former defense secretary, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Carlucci.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Many of the military experts whom I consulted on this agreed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to spend more money in the future on military technology and on greater mobility, greater airlift, greater sealift, the B-22 airplane.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to do some things that are quite costly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I simply don’t believe we can afford nor do we need to keep 150,000 troops in Europe given how much the Red Army, now under the control of Russia, has been cut, the arms control agreement concluded between Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush and Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Yeltsin, something I have applauded.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we need 150,000 troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me make one other point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush talked about taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He didn’t tell you that he vetoed a middle class tax cut because it would be paid for by raising taxes on the wealthy and vetoed an investment tax credit paid for by raising taxes on the wealthy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s 10 cents a year cumulative.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It finally gets to 50 cents at the end of the 5th year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think “punish” is the wrong word.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Again, see, I didn’t create this problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’re trying to solve it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, if you study our international competitors, some of our international competitors collect up to $3.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: 50 a gallon in taxes, and they use that money to build infrastructure and to create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We collect 35 cents, and we don’t have it to spend.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I know it’s not popular, and I understand the nature of your question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But the people who will be helped the most by it are the working people who will get the jobs created because of this tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Why do we have to do it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Because we have so mismanaged our country over the years, and it is now time to pay the fiddler.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And if we don’t, we will be spending our children’s money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have spent $4 trillion worth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: An incredible number of young people are active in supporting my effort because they are deeply concerned that we have taken the American dream from them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s fitting that we’re on the campus of a university tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: These young people, when they get out of this wonderful university, will have difficulty finding a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to clean this mess up, leave this country in good shape, and pass on the American dream to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to collect the taxes to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If there’s a fairer way, I’m all ears –aah.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But–but–see, let me make it very clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If people don’t have the stomach to fix these problems, I think it’s a good time to face it, November.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If they do, then they will have heard the harsh reality of what we have to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’m not playing Lawrence Welk music tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot has confronted this deficit issue, but I think it’s important to point out that we really have 2 deficits in America, not one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have a budget deficit in the federal government, but we also have an investment, a jobs, an income deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: People are working harder for less money than they were making 10 years ago, 2- 3rds of our people–a $1600 drop in average income in just the last 2 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The problem I have with the Perot prescription is that almost all economists who’ve looked at it say that if you cut the deficit this much this quick it will increase unemployment, it will slow down the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I think we shouldn’t do it that quickly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have a disciplined reduction in the deficit of 50 % over the next 4 years, but first get incentives to invest in this economy, put the American people back to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to invest and grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: 9 Nobel Prize-winning economists and 500 others, including numerous Republican and Democratic business executives, have endorsed this approach because it offers the best hope to put America back to work and get our incomes rising instead of falling.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Your question was on fairness.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just disagree with Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Perot.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe it is fair to slap a 50-cent-a-gallon tax over whatever many years on the people that have to drive for a living, people that go long distances.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we need to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You see, I have a fundamental difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I agree with what he’s talking about in trying to get this spending down and the discipline, although I think we ought to totally exempt Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But he’s talking tough medicine, and I think that’s good.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I disagree with the tax-and-spend philosophy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You see, I don’t think we need to tax more and spend more, and then say that’s going to make the problem better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m afraid that’s what I think I’m hearing from Governor Clinton.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe what you need to do is some of what Ross is talking about: control the growth of mandatory spending and get taxes down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s mentioned some ways to do it–and I agree with those.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been talking about getting a capital gains cut forever, and his friends in Congress have been telling me that’s a tax break for the rich.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It would stimulate investment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m for an investment tax allowance; I’m for a tax break for first- time homebuyers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And with this new Congress coming in, gridlock will be gone, and I’ll sit down with them and say let’s get this done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I do not want to go the tax-and-spend route.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I assume she was supportive of the decision on McDonnell Douglas, I assume she was supporting me on the decision to sell those airplanes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s a good decision–took a little heat for it, but I think it was the correct decision to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we worked it out, and indeed we’re moving forward all around the world in a much more peaceful way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So that one we came away with in creating jobs for the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would simply say to her, look, take a look at what the president has proposed on job retraining.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When you cut back on defense spending, some people are going to be thrown out of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you throw another 50,000 kids on the street because of cutting recklessly in troop levels, you’re going to put a lot more out of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would say to them, look at the job retraining programs that we’re proposing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Therein is the best answer to her.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And another one is: stimulate investment and savings.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, we’ve got big economic problems, but we are not coming apart at the seams; we’re ready for a recovery.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: With interest rates down and inflation down, the cruelest tax of all, caught up in a global slowdown right now, that that will change if you go with the programs I’ve talked about and if you help with job retraining and education.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am a firm believer that our America 2000 education problem is the answer–a little longer run; it’s going to take awhile to educate.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it is a good program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So her best help for short term is job retraining, if she was thrown out of work at a defense plant.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But tell her it’s not all that gloomy; we’re the US, we faced tough problems before.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Look at the misery index when the Democrats had both the White House and the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was just right through the roof.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, we can do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the way to do better is not to tax and spend but to retrain, get that control of the mandatory spending programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m much more optimistic about this country than some.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Defense industries are going to have to convert to civilian industries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Many of them are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And the sooner they start, the sooner they’ll finish.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And there will be a significant transition.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And it’s very important that we not continue to let our industrial base deteriorate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We had someone who I’m sure regrets said it in the president’s staff said he didn’t care whether we made potato chips or computer chips.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, anybody that thinks about it cares a great deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Number one, you make more making computer chips than potato chips; and, number 2, 19 out of 20 computer chips that we have in this country now come from Japan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve given away whole industries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So as we phase these industries over, there’s a whole of intellectual talent in these industries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: A lot of these people in industries can be converted to the industries of tomorrow, and that’s where the high-paying jobs are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We need to have a very carefully thought through phase-over.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, see, we practice 19th century capitalism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The rest of the world practices 21st century capitalism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I can’t handle that in a minute, but I hope we can get back into it later.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: In the rest of the world, the countries and the businesses would be working together to make this transition in an intelligent way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We must have a transition plan to plan to convert from a defense to a domestic economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: No other nation would have cut defense as much as we already have without that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are 200,000 people unemployed in California alone because we have cut defense without planning to retrain them and to reinvest in the technologies of the future here at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is what I want to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This administration may say they have a plan, but the truth is they have not even released all the money, the paltry sum of money, that Congress appropriated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to take very dollar by which we reduce defense and reinvest it in technologies for the 21st century–in new transportation, in communication, in environmental clean-up technologies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let’s put the American people to work, and let’s build the kind of high-tech, high-wage, high-growth economy that the American people deserve.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Step one, the American people send me up there, the day after election, I’ll get with congressional–we won’t even wait till inauguration, and I’ll ask the president to help me and I’ll ask his staff to help me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And we will start putting together teams to put together–to take all the plans that exist and do something with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Please understand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: There are great plans lying all over Washington nobody ever executes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s like having a blueprint for a house you never built.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You don’t have anywhere to sleep.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now our challenge is to take these things, do something with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Step one, we want to put America back to work, clean up the small business problem, have one task force at work on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The second, you’ve got your big companies that are in trouble, including the defense industries–have another one on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Have a 3rd task force on new industries of the future to make sure we nail those for our country and they don’t wind up in Europe and Asia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Convert from 19th to 21st century capitalism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: See, we have an adversarial relationship between government and business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Our international competitors that are cleaning our plate have an intelligent relationship between government and business, and a supportive relationship.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then have another task force on crime because, next to jobs, our people are concerned about their safety.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Health care, schools–one on the debt and deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And finally in that 90- day period before the inauguration, put together the framework for the town hall and give the American people a Christmas present.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Show them by Christmas the first cut at these plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: By the time Congress comes into session to go to work, have those plans ready to go in front of Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then get off to a flying start in ’93 to execute these plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, there are people in this room and people on this stage who’ve been in meetings when I would sit there and say, “Is this the one we’re going to talk about or do something about?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: ” Well, obviously, my orientation is let’s go do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, put together your plans by Christmas, be ready to go when Congress goes, nail these things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Small business–you’ve got to have capital, you’ve got to credit, and many of them need mentors or coaches.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And we can create more jobs there in a hurry than any other place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This country desperately needs a jobs program, and my first priority would be to pass a jobs program, to introduce it on the first day I was inaugurated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I would meet with the leaders of the Congress, with all the newly elected members of the Congress and as many others with whom I could meet between the time of the election and the inauguration, and we would present a jobs program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Then we would present a plan to control health care costs and phase in health care coverage for all Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Until we control health care costs, we’re not going to control the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is the number one culprit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But first we must have an aggressive jobs program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I live in a state where manufacturing job growth has far outpaced the nation in the last few years, where we have created more private sector jobs since Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush has been president than have been created in the entire rest of the country, where Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush’s labor secretary said job growth has been enormous.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve done it in Arkansas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Give me a chance to create these kind of jobs in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I know we can.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got the plan announced for what we can do for small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve already put forward things that’ll get this country working fast, some of which have been echoed here tonight–investment tax allowance, capital gains reduction, more on research and development, tax credit for first-time home buyers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What I’m going to do is say to Jim Baker when this campaign is over, all right, let’s sit down now, you do in domestic affairs what you’ve done in foreign affairs, be kind of the economic coordinator of all the domestic side of the House, and that includes all the economic side, all the training side, and bring this program together.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have a new Congress, and we’re going to say to them, you’ve listened to the voters the way we have.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Nobody wants gridlock anymore, and so let’s get the program through.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I believe it’ll work because, as Ross said, we got the plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The plans are all over Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve put ours together in something called the Agenda for American Renewal, and it makes sense, it’s sensible, it creates jobs, it gets to the base of the kind of jobs we need.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I’ll just be asking for support to get that put into effect.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me say that I think that we might ought to review the terms, the way it works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But frankly, I don’t think that’s the problem today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have low interest rates today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: At least we have low interest rates that the Fed can control.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our long-term interest rates are still pretty high because of our deficit and because of our economic performance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And there was a terrible reaction internationally to Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush saying he was going to give us 4 more years of trickle-down economics–another across-the- board tax cut and most of it going to the wealthy, with no real guarantee of investment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I think the important thing–the important thing– is to use the powers the president does have on the assumption that, given the condition of this economy, we’re going to keep interest rates down if we have the discipline to increase investment and reduce the debt at the same time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is my commitment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think the American people are ready for action.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think Congress is hungry for someone who will work with them instead of manipulate them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Someone who will not veto a bill that has an investment tax credit, middle class tax relief, research and development tax credits as Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush has done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Give me a chance to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have to worry in the near term about the Federal Reserve.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Their policies so far, it seems to me, are pretty sound.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think the Fed ought to be put under the Executive Branch.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is a separation there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think that’s fine.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Alan Greenspan is respected.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve had some arguments with him about the speed in which we might have lowered interest rates, but Governor Clinton, he talks about the reaction to the markets.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There was a momentary fear that he might win and that the markets went phwee, down like that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I don’t think we can judge on, the stock market has been strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s been very strong since I’ve been president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And they recognize we got great difficulties, but they’re also much more optimistic than the pessimists we have up here tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In terms of vetoing tax bills, you’re darn right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am going to protect the American taxpayer against the spend and tax Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m going to keep on vetoing them, because I don’t think we’re taxed too little.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the government’s spending too much.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So Governor Clinton can label it tax for the rich or anything he wants.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to protect the working man by continuing to veto, and to threaten to veto until we get this new Congress, and then we’re going to move forward on our plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Iâ€™ve got to protect them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Keep the Federal Reserve independent, but let’s live in a world of reality.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We live in a global economy, not a national economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: These interest rates we have now don’t make any sense.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have a four trillion dollar debt, and only in America would you finance seventy percent of it five years or less.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So seventy percent of our debt is five years or less.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s very interest sensitive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have a four percent gap between what we pay for treasuries, and what Germany pays for one to five year treasuries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That gap is going to close, because the Arabs, the Japanese and folks in this country are going to start buying German treasuries because they can get more money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Every time our interest rates go up one percent, that adds 28 billion dollars to the deficit or to the debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Whichever place you put it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We are sitting on a ticking time bomb folks, because we have totally mismanaged our country, and we had better get it back under control.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Just think in your own business, if you had all of your long term problems financed short term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’d go broke in a hurry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Again, if you’re not rich, you’re not a superpower.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So we have two that I’d put as number one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I have number 1 and 1A.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: One is we’ve got to have the money to be able to pay for defense, and we’ve got to manufacture here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Believe it or not folks, you can’t ship it all overseas, you’ve got to make it here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And you can’t convert from potato chips to airplanes in an emergency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: See, Willow Run could be converted from cars to airplanes in World War II because it was here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to make things here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You can’t ship them overseas anymore.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I hope we can talk more about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Second thing, on priorities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to help Russia succeed in its revolution and all of its republics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: When we think of Russia, remember we’re thinking of many countries, now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to help them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s pennies on the dollar compared to renewing the cold war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Third, we’ve got all kinds of agreements on paper, and some that are being executed on getting rid of nuclear warheads.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Russia and its republics are out of control or at best in weak control right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s a very unstable situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got every rich Middle Eastern country over there trying to buy nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: As you well know.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And that will lead to another five star migraine headache down the road.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We really need to nail down the big intercontinental ballistic missiles, the ones that can hit us from Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve focused on the tactical.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve made real progress there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got some agreement on the nuclear, but we don’t have those things put away yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The sooner the better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So, in terms of priorities, we’ve got to be financially strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Number two, we’ve got to take care of this missile situation and try to get the nuclear war behind us and give this thing very high priority.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And number three, we need to help and support Russia and the republics in every possible way to become democratic capitalistic societies, and not just sit back and let those countries continue in turmoil.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Because they could go back worse than things used to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And believe me there are a lot of old boys in the K.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: and the military that liked it better the way it used to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In order to keep America the strongest nation in the world, we need some continuity and some change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are three fundamental challenges.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First of all, the world is still a dangerous and uncertain place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need a new military and a new national security policy equal to the challenges of a post cold war era, a smaller permanent military force, but one that is more mobile, well trained with high technology equipment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to continue the negotiations to reduce the nuclear arsenals in the Soviet Union, the former Soviet Union, and the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to stop this proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Second, we have to face that in this world, economic security is a whole lot of national security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Our dollar’s at an all time low against some foreign currencies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re weak in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We must rebuild America’s strength at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And finally, we ought to be promoting the democratic impulses around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Democracies are our partners.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They don’t go to war with each other.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They’re reliable friends in the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: National security, economic strength, democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, we still are the envy of the world in terms of our military.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s no question about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re the envy of the world in terms of our economy, despite the difficulties we’re having.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s no question about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our exports are dramatically up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I might say to Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Perot, I can understand why you might have missed it, because there’s so much fascination with trivia, but I worked out a deal with Boris Yeltsin to eliminate, get rid of entirely, the most destabilizing weapons of all, the SS-18, the intercontinental ballistic missile.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, that’s been done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And thank God, it has, because the parents of these young people around here go to bed at night without the same fear of nuclear war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We made dramatic progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so, we’ve got a good military.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: the question, to sort of get a new military, get the best in the world, we got it, and theyâ€™re keeping the peace, and they’re respected around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’re more respected because of the way we have conducted ourselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t listen to the nuclear freeze crowd.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We said, “Peace through strength,” and it worked and the cold war is over.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And America understands that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we’re so, turned so inward we don’t understand the global picture.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we are helping democracy, Ross.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Freedom Support Act is something I got through the Congress, and it’s a very good thing, because it does exactly what you say, and I think you agree with that, to help Russian democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to keep on doing that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think our relationships with China are important and I don’t want to isolate China, but I think it is a mistake for us to do what this Administration did when all those kids went out there carrying the Statue of Liberty in Tiananmen Square.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr Bush sent two people in secret to toast the Chinese leaders and basically tell them not to worry about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They rewarded him by opening negotiations with Iran to transfer nuclear technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That was their response to that sort of action.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now that the voices in the Congress and throughout the country have insisted that we do something about China, look at what has happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: China has finally agreed to stop sending us products made with prison labor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Not because we coddled them, but because the Administration was pushed into doing something about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And recently the Chinese have announced they are going to lower some barriers to our products, which they ought to do since they have a 15 billion dollar trade surplus with the United States under Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The second biggest surplus next to Japan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I would be firm.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I would say if you want to continue as Most Favored Nation status for your government owned industries as well as your private ones, observe human rights in the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Open your society.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Recognize the legitimacy of those kids that were carrying the Statue of Liberty.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If we can stand up for our economics, we ought to be able to preserve the democratic interests of the people of China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And over the long run they will be more reliable partners.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, the Administration was the first major country to stand up to the abuse in Tiananmen Square.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We are the one that worked out the prison labor deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We are the ones that lowered the barrier to products with Carla Hill’s negotiation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am the one that said let’s keep the M.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: because you see China moving towards a free market economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: To do what the Congress and Governor Clinton is suggesting, you’d isolate and ruin Hong Kong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They are making some progress, not enough for us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We were the first ones to put sanctions on.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We still have them on, on some things.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But Governor Clinton’s philosophy is isolate them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He says don’t do it, but the policies he’s expounding of putting conditions on M.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: and kind of humiliating them is not the way you make the kind of progress we are getting.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve stood up with these people, and I understand what you have to do to be strong in this situation, and it’s moving, not as fast as we’d like.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But you isolate China and turn them inward, and then we’ve made a tremendous mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m not going to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve had to fight a lot of people that were saying human rights, and weâ€™re the ones that put the sanctions on and stood for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he can insult General Scowcroft if he wants to.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They didn’t go over to coddle.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He went over to say we must make the very changes they’re making now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: All right, it’s huge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: China, is a huge country, broken into many provinces.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It has some very elderly leaders that will not be around too much longer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Capitalism is growing and thriving across big portions of China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Asia will be our largest trading partner in the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It will be a growing and a closer relationship.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have a delicate, tight-wire walk that we must go through at the present time to make sure that we do not cozy up to tyrants, to make sure that they don’t get the impression that they can suppress their people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But time is our friend there, because their leaders will change in not too many years, worst case, and their country is making great progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: One last point on the missiles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want the American people to be confused.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have written agreements and we have some missiles that have been destroyed, but we have a huge number of intercontinental ballistic missiles that are still in place in Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The fact that you have an agreement is one thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Till they’re destroyed, some crazy person can either sell them or use them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Ann, both of them are very complicated situations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I vowed something because I learned something from Vietnam.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am not going to commit US forces until I know what the mission is, till the military tell me that it can be completed, and till I know how they can come out.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We are helping.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: American airplanes are helping today on humanitarian relief for Sarajevo.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is America that’s in the lead in helping with humanitarian relief for Somalia.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But when you go to put somebody else’s son or daughter into war, I think you got to be a little bit careful and you have to be sure that there’s a military plan that can do this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You have ancient ethnic rivalries that have cropped up as Yugoslavia’s dissolved or getting dissolved, and it isn’t going to be solved by sending in the 82nd Airborne, and I’m not going to do that as commander-in-chief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am going to stand by and use the moral persuasion of the US to get satisfaction in terms of prison camps, and we’re making some progress there, and in terms of getting humanitarian relief in there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And right now, as you know, the US took the lead in a no-fly operation up there in– no- fly order up in the United Nations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re working through the international organizations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s one thing I learned by forging that tremendous and greatly–highly successful coalition against Saddam Hussein, the dictator.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Use–work internationally to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am very concerned about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am concerned about ethnic cleansing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
