transcript_turns.text: I am concerned about a tax on Muslims, for example, over there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I must stop short of using American force until I know how those young men and women are going to get out of there as well as get in, know what the mission is, and define it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think I’m on the right track.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think if we learned anything in Vietnam is you first commit this nation before you commit the troops to the battlefield.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We cannot send our people all over the world to solve every problem that comes up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This is basically a problem that is a primary concern to the European Community.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Certainly we care about the people, we care about the children, we care about the tragedy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But it is inappropriate for us, just because there’s a problem somewhere around the world, to take the sons and daughters of working people–and make no mistake about it, our all- volunteer armed force is not made up of the sons and daughters of the beautiful people; it’s the working folks who send their sons and daughters to war, with a few exceptions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s very unlike World War II, when FDR’s sons flew missions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Everybody went.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s a different world now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s very important that we not just, without thinking it through, just rush to every problem in the world and have our people torn to pieces.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I agree that we cannot commit ground forces to become involved in the quagmire of Bosnia or in the tribal wars of Somalia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I think that it’s important to recognize that there are things that can be done short of that, and that we do have interests there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There are, after all, 2 million refugees now because of the problems in what was Yugoslavia, the largest number since World War II, and there may be hundreds of thousands of people who will starve or freeze to death in this winter.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The US should try to work with its allies and stop it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I urged the president to support this air cover, and he did–and I applaud that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I applaud the no-fly zone, and I know that he’s going back to the United Nations to try to get authority to enforce it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we should stiffen the embargo on the Belgrade government, and I think we have to consider whether or not we should lift the arms embargo now on the Bosnians, since they are in no way in a fair fight with a heavily armed opponent bent on ethnic cleansing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can’t get involved in the quagmire, but we must do what we can.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: A family involves at least one parent, whether natural or adoptive or foster, and children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: A good family is a place where love and discipline and good values are transmuted from the elders to the children, a place where people turn for refuge, and where they know they’re the most important people in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: America has a lot of families that are in trouble today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There’s been a lot of talk about family values in this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I know a lot about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I was born to a widowed mother who gave me family values, and grandparents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve seen the family values of my people in Arkansas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve seen the family values of all these people in America who are out there killing themselves working harder for less in a country that’s had the worst economic years in 50 years and the first decline in industrial production ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think the president owes it to family values to show that he values America’s families, whether they’re people on welfare you’re trying to move from welfare to work, the working poor whom I think deserve a tax break to lift them above poverty if they’ve got a child in the house and working 40 hours a week, working families who deserve a fair tax system and the opportunity for constant retraining; they deserve a strong economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think they deserve a family and medical leave act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Seventy-two other nations have been able to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush vetoed it twice because he says we can’t do something seventy-two other countries do, even though there was a small business exemption.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So with all the talk about family values, I know about family values — I wouldn’t be here without them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The best expression of my family values is that tonight’s my 17th wedding anniversary, and I’d like to close my question by just wishing my wife a happy anniversary, and thank you, my daughter, for being here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I would say that one meeting that made a profound impression on me was when the mayors of the big cities, including the mayor of Los Angeles, a Democrat, came to see me, and they unanimously said the decline in urban America stems from the decline in the American family.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I do think we need to strengthen family.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When Barbara holds an AIDS baby, she’s showing a certain compassion for family; when she reads to children, the same thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe that discipline and respect for the law — all of these things should be taught to children, not in our schools, but families have to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m appalled at the highest outrageous numbers of divorces — it happens in families, it’s happened in ours.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it’s gotten too much.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I just think that we ought to do everything we can to respect the American family.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It can be a single-parent family.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Those mothers need help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And one way to do it is to get these deadbeat fathers to pay their obligations to these mothers — that will help strengthen the American family.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And there’s a whole bunch of other things that I can’t click off in this short period of time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If I had to solve all the problems that face this country and I could be granted one wish as we started down the trail to rebuild the job base, the schools and so on and so forth, I would say a strong family unit in every home, where every child is loved, nurtured, and encouraged.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: A little child before they’re 18 months learns to think well of himself or herself or poorly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They develop a positive or negative self- image.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: At a very early age they learn how to learn.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If we have children who are not surrounded with love and affection — you see, I look at my grandchildren and wonder if they’ll ever learn to walk because they’re always in someone’s arms.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I think, my gosh, wouldn’t it be wonderful if every child had that love and support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But they don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We will not be a great country unless we have a strong family unit in every home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I think you can use the White House as a bully pulpit to stress the importance of these little children, particularly in their young and formative years, to mold these little precious pieces of clay so that they, too, can live rich full lives when they’re grown.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, I don’t think that’s the right answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe legalizing narcotics is the answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just don’t believe that’s the answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do believe that there’s some fairly good news out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The use of cocaine, for example, by teenagers is dramatically down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we’ve got to keep fighting on this war against drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re doing a little better in interdiction.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Many of the countries below that used to say, well, this is the US’ problem — if you’d get the demand down, then we wouldn’t have the problem — are working cooperatively with the DEA and the military.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re using the military more now in terms of interdiction.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our funding for recovery is up, recovering the addicts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Where we’re not making the progress, Sander, is in — we’re making it in teenagers, and thank God, because I thought what Ross said was most appropriate about these families and these children.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But where we’re not making it is with the confirmed addicts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll tell you one place that’s working well, and that is the private sector — Jim Burke and this task force that he has, you may know about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll tell the American people, but this man said I’ll get you a million dollars a day in pro bono advertising, something that’s very hard for the government to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he went out and he did it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And people are beginning to educate through this program, teaching these kids you shouldn’t use drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So we’re still in the fight.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I must tell you, I think legalization of narcotics, or something of that nature, in the face of the medical evidence, would be totally counterproductive.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I oppose it, and I’m going to stand up and continue to oppose it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Anytime you think you want to legalize drugs, go to a neonatal unit — if you can get in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re between 100 and 200% capacity up and down the East Coast.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And the reason is crack babies being born, babies in the hospital 42 days.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Typical cost to you and me is $125,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Again and again and again, the mother disappears in 3 days, and the child becomes a ward of the state because he’s permanently and genetically damaged.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Just look at those little children, and if anybody can even think about legalizing drugs, they’ve lost me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, let’s look at priorities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: You know, we went on the Libyan raid — do you remember that one?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: — because we were worried to death that Gaddafi might be building up chemical weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got chemical warfare being conducted against our children on the streets in this country all day every day, and we don’t have the will to stamp it out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, again, if I get up there, if you send me, we’re going to have some blunt talks about this, and we’re really going to get down in the trenches and say, is this one you want to talk about or fix, because talk won’t do it, folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: There are guys that couldn’t get a job third shift in a Dairy Queen driving BMWs and Mercedes selling drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And these old boys are not going to quit easy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Like Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot, I have held crack babies in my arms.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I know more about this, I think, than anybody else up here because I have a brother who’s a recovering drug addict.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m very proud of him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I can tell you this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If drugs were legal, I don’t think he’d be alive today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I am adamantly opposed to legalizing drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He is alive today because of the criminal justice system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What should we do?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First, we ought to prevent more of this on the street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thirty years ago, there were three policemen for every crime.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now there are three crimes for every policeman.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need a hundred thousand more police on the street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have a plan for that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, we ought to have treatment on demand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thirdly, we ought to have boot camps for first-time nonviolent offenders so they can get discipline and treatment and education and get reconnected to the community before they’re severed and sent to prison, where they can learn how to be first class criminals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There is a crime bill that, lamentably, was blocked from passage once again, mostly by Republicans in the US Senate, which would have addressed some of these problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That crime bill is going to be one of my highest priorities next January if I become president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This is a relevant question here tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The first thing I’d do is, during political campaigns, I would urge everybody to stop trying to split this country into fragments and appeal to the differences between us and then wonder why the melting pot is all broken to pieces after November the 3rd.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We are all in this together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We ought to love one another because united teams win and divided teams lose.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And if we can’t love one another, we ought to get along with one another.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And if you can’t get there, just recognize we’re all stuck with one another because nobody’s going anywhere, right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, that ought to get everybody back up to let’s get along together and make it work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Our diversity is a strength.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve turned it into a weakness.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now again, the White House is a bully pulpit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I think whoever is in the White House should just make it absolutely unconscionable and inexcusable, and if anybody’s in the middle of a speech at, you know, one of these conventions, I would expect the candidate to go out and lift him off the stage if he starts preaching hate — because we don’t have time for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: See, our differences are our strengths.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have got to pull together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: In athletics, we know it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: See, divided teams lose; united teams win.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We have got to unite and pull together, and there’s nothing we can’t do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But if we sit around blowing all this energy out the window on racial strife and hatred, we are stuck with a sure loser because we have been a melting pot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’re becoming more and more of a melting pot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let’s make it a strength, not a weakness.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I grew up in the segregated South, thankfully raised by a grandfather with almost no formal education but with a heart of gold who taught me early that all people were equal in the eyes of God.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I saw the winds of hatred divide people and keep the people of my state poorer than they would have been, spiritually and economically.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve done everything I could in my public life to overcome racial divisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have a person to waste in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We are being murdered economically because we have too many drop-outs, we have too many low birthweight babies, we have too many drug addicts as kids, we have too much violence, we are too divided by race, by income, by region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I have devoted a major portion of this campaign to going across this country and looking for opportunities to go to white groups and African American groups and Latino groups and Asian American groups and say the same thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If the American people cannot be brought together, we can’t turn this country around.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If we can come together, nothing can stop us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think Governor Clinton is committed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do think it’s fair to note — he can rebut it — but Arkansas is one of the few states that doesn’t have any civil rights legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve tried to use the White House as a bully pulpit, speaking out against discrimination.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We passed two very forward-looking civil rights bills.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not going to be all done by legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I do think that you need to make an appeal every time you can to eliminate racial divisions and discrimination, and I’ll keep on doing that and pointing to some legislative accomplishment to back it up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have to take ten seconds here at the end — the red light isn’t on yet — to say to Ross Perot, please don’t say to the DEA agents on the street that we don’t have the will to fight drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Please.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have watched these people — the same for our local law enforcement people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re backing up at every way we possibly can.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But maybe you meant that some in the country don’t have the will to fight it, but those that are out there on the front line, as you know — you’ve been a strong backer of law enforcement — really — I just want to clear that up –have the will to fight it, and, frankly, some of them are giving their lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Coming from the political process.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have increased funding for AIDS.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve doubled it on research and on every other aspect of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My request for this year was $4.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 9 billion for AIDS — ten times as much per AIDS victim as per cancer victim.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think that we’re showing the proper compassion and concern.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I can’t tell you where it’s coming from, but I am very much concerned about AIDS and I believe that we’ve got the best researchers in the world out there at NIH working the problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re funding them Ã¢â‚¬â€œ I wish there was more money — but we’re funding them far more than any time in the past, and we’re going to keep on doing that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I was a little disappointed in Magic because he came to me and I said, “Now if you see something we’re not doing, get ahold of me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Call me, let me know.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” He went to one meeting, and then we heard that he was stepping down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So he’s replaced by Mary Fisher who electrified the Republican Convention by talking about the compassion and the concern that we feel.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was a beautiful moment and I think she’ll do a first-class job on that commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I think the appeal is yes, we care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the other thing is part of AIDS — it’s one of the few diseases where behavior matters.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I once called on somebody, “Well, change your behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Is the behavior you’re using prone to cause AIDS?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Change the behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” Next thing I know, one of these ACT UP groups is out saying, “Bush ought to change his behavior.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” You can’t talk about it rationally.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The extremes are hurting the AIDS cause.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: To go into a Catholic mass in a beautiful cathedral in New York under the cause of helping in AIDS and start throwing condoms around in the mass, I’m sorry, I think it sets back the cause.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We cannot move to the extreme.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to continue everything we can at the federal and the local level.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Barbara I think is doing a superb job in destroying the myth about AIDS.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And all of us are in this fight together, all of us care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Do not go to the extreme.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: First, I think Mary Fisher was a great choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’re lucky to have her heading the commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, I think one thing that if I were sent to do the job, I would sit down with FDA, look at exactly where we are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then I would really focus on let’s get these things out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you’re going to die, you don’t have to go through this ten-year cycle that FDA goes through on new drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Believe me, people with AIDS are more than willing to take that risk.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And we could be moving out to the human population a whole lot faster than we are on some of these new drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So I would think we can expedite the problem there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let me go back a minute to racial divisiveness.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The all- time low in our country was the Judge Thomas-Anita Hill hearings, and those senators ought to be hanging their heads in shame for what they did there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: 2nd thing, there are not many times in your life when you get to talk to a whole country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But let me just say to all of America: if you hate people, I don’t want your vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s how strongly I feel about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Over 150,000 Americans have died of AIDS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well over a million and a quarter Americans are HIV-positive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to put one person in charge of the battle against AIDS to cut across all the agencies that deal with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to accelerate the drug approval process.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to fully fund the act named for that wonderful boy Ryan White to make sure we’re doing everything we can on research and treatment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the president should lead a national effort to change behavior, to keep our children alive in the schools, responsible behavior to keep people alive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is a matter of life and death.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have worked in my state to reduce teen pregnancy and illness among children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I know it’s tough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The reason Magic Johnson resigned from the AIDS Commission is because the statement you heard tonight from Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush is the longest and best statement he’s made about it in public.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I am proud of what we did at the Democratic Convention, putting 2 HIV-positive people on the platform, and I am proud of the leadership that I’m going to bring to this country in dealing with the AIDS crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Two ways.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Number one, if I get there, it will be a very unusual and historical event — –because the people, not the special interests, put me there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I will have a unique mandate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I have said again and again, and this really upsets the establishment in Washington, that we’re going to inform the people in detail on the issues through an electronic town hall so that they really know what’s going on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They will want to do what’s good for our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, all these fellows with thousand-dollar suits and alligator shoes running up and down the halls of Congress that make policy now — the lobbyists, the PAC guys, the foreign lobbyists, and what-have-you, they’ll be over there in the Smithsonian, you know — — because we’re going to get rid of them, and the Congress will be listening to the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And the American people are willing to have fair, shared sacrifice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’re not as stupid as Washington thinks they are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The American people are bright, intelligent, caring, loving people who want a great country for their children and grandchildren.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And they will make those sacrifices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So I welcome that challenge, and just watch — — because if the American people send me there, we’ll get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now, everybody will faint in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They’ve never seen anything happen in that town.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: This is a town where the White House says, Congress did it; Congress says, the White House did it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I’m sitting there and saying, well, who else could be around, you know?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Then when they get off by themselves, they say nobody did it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And yet the cash register’s empty and it used to have our money, the taxpayers’ money, in it, and we didn’t get the results.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: No, we’ll get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Ross, that’s a great speech, but it’s not quite that simple.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I mean, look at the facts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Both parties in Washington, the president and the Congress, have cut Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The average senior citizen is spending a higher percentage of income on health care today than they were in 1965, before Medicare came in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The president’s got another proposal to require them to pay $400 a year more for the next 5 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But if you don’t have the guts to control costs by changing the insurance system and taking on the bureaucracies and the regulation of health care in the private and public sector, you can’t fix this problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Costs will continue to spiral.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And just remember this, folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: A lot of folks on Medicare are out there every day making the choice between food and medicine; not poor enough for Medicare-Medicaid, not wealthy enough to buy their medicine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve met them, people like Mary Annie and Edward Davis in Nashua, New Hampshire.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: All over this country, they cannot even buy medicine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So let’s be careful.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When we talk about cutting health care costs, let’s start with the insurance companies and the people that are making a killing instead of making our people healthy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, first place, I’d like to clear up something because every 4 years, the Democrats go around and say, Republicans are going to cut Social Security and Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They started it again.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m the president that stood up and said, don’t mess with Social Security, and I’m not going to and we haven’t and we are not going to go after the Social Security recipient.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have one difference with Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Perot on that because I don’t think we need to touch Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What we do need to do, though, is control the growth of these mandatory programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And Ross properly says, okay, there’s some pain in that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But Governor Clinton refuses to touch that, simply refuses.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So what we’ve got to do is control it, let it grow for inflation, let it grow for the amount of new people added, population, and then hold the line.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I believe that is the way you get the deficit down, not by the tax-and-spend program that we hear every 4 years, whether it’s Mondale, Dukakis, whoever else it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just don’t believe we ought to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So hold the line on Social Security and put a cap on the growth of the mandatory program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush made that charge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I thought the Oregon plan should at least have been allowed to be tried because at least the people in Oregon were trying to do something.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me go back to the main point, Sandy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush is trying to run against Lyndon Johnson and Jimmy Carter and everybody in the world but me in this race.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have proposed a managed competition plan for health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I will say again: you cannot control health care costs simply by cutting Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Look what’s happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The federal government has cut Medicare and Medicaid in the last few years, states have cut Medicaid — we’ve done it in Arkansas under budget pressures.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But what happens?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: More and more people get on the rolls as poverty increases.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If you don’t control the health care costs of the entire system, you cannot get control of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Look at our program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We set up a national ceiling on health care costs tied to inflation and population growth set by health care providers, not by the government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We provide for managed competition, not government models, in every states.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we control private and public health care costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, just a few days ago a bipartisan commission of Republicans and Democrats — more Republicans than Democrats — said my plan will save the average family $1200 a year more than the Bush plan will by the year 2000, $2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: 2 trillion in the next 12 years, $400 billion a year by the end of this decade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got a plan to control health care costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But you can’t just do it by cutting Medicare; you have to take on the insurance companies, the bureaucracies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you have to have cost controls, yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But keep in mind we are spending 30% more on health care than any country in the world, any country, and yet we have 35 million people uninsured, we have no preventing and primary care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The Oregon plan is a good start if the federal government is going to continue to abandon its responsibilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I say if Germany can cover everybody and keep costs under inflation, if Hawaii can cover 98% of their people at lower health care costs than the rest of us, if Rochester, New York, can do it with two-thirds of the cost of the rest of it, America can do it, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m tired of being told we can’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I say we can.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We can do better, and we must.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I don’t have time in 30 seconds, or whatever — a minute — to talk about our health care reform plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Oregon plan made some good sense, but it’s easy to dismiss the concerns of the disabled.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As president I have to be sure that those waivers, which we’re approving all over the place, are covered under the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Maybe we can work it out.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the Americans with Disabilities Act, speaking about sound and sensible civil rights legislation, was the most foremost piece of legislation passed in modern times, and so we do have something more than a technical problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Governor Clinton clicked off the things — he’s going to take on insurance companies and bureaucracies.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He failed to take on somebody else — the malpractice suit people, those that bring these lawsuits against — these frivolous trial lawyers’ lawsuits that are running the costs of medical care up 25 to 50 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he refuses to put anything, controls, on these crazy lawsuits.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you want to help somebody, don’t run the costs up by making doctors have to have 5 or 6 tests where one would do for fear of being sued, or have somebody along the highway not stop to pick up a guy and help him because he’s afraid a trial lawyer will come along and sue him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re suing each other too much and caring for each other too little.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We got the most expensive health care system in the world; it ranks behind 15 other nations when we come to life expectancy, and 22 other nations when we come to infant mortality.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: So we don’t have the best.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Pretty simple, folks — if you’re paying more and you don’t have the best, if all else fails go copy the people who have the best who spend less, right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, we can do better than that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Again, we’ve got plans lying all over the place in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Nobody ever implements them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Now I’m back to square one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: If you want to stop talking about it and do it, then I’ll be glad to go up there and we’ll get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: But if you just want to keep the music going, just stay traditional this next time around, and 4 years from now you’ll have everybody blaming everybody else for a bad health care system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Talk is cheap; words are plentiful, deeds are precious.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Let’s get on with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Well, it’s been a privilege to be able to talk to the American people tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I make no bones about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I love this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I love the principle it’s founded on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I love the people here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t like to see the country’s principles violated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I don’t like to see the people in a deteriorating economy in a deteriorating country because our government has lost touch with the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: The people in Washington are good people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We just have a bad system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to change the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: It’s time to do it because we have run up so much debt that time is no longer our friend.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to put our house in order.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: When you go to bed tonight, look at your children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Think of their dreams.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Think of your dreams as a child and ask yourself, isn’t it time to stop talking about it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Isn’t it time to stop creating images?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Isn’t it time to do it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Aren’t you sick of being treated like an unprogrammed robot?

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: Every 4 years, they send you all kinds of messages to tell you how to vote and then go back to business as usual.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They told you at the tax and budget summit that if you agreed to a tax increase, we could balance the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They didn’t tell you that that same year they increased spending $1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: 83 for every dollar we increased taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: That’s Washington in a nutshell right there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: In the final analysis, I’m doing this for your children when you look at them tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: There’s another group that I feel very close to, and these at the men and women who fought on the battlefield, the children — the families — of the ones who died and the people who left parts of their bodies over there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’d never ask you to do anything for me, but I owe you this, and I’m doing it for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And I can’t tell you what it means to me at these rallies when I see you and you come up and the look in your eyes — and I know how you feel and you know how I feel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And then I think of the older people who are retired.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They grew up in the Depression.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: They fought and won World War II.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: We owe you a debt we can never repay you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: And the greatest repayment I can ever give is to recreate the American dream for your children and grandchildren.

transcript_turns.speaker: Ross Perot
transcript_turns.text: I’ll give you everything I have, if you want me to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to thank the people of St.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Louis and Washington University, the Presidential Debate Commission and all those who made this night possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I’d like to thank those of you who are watching.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Most of all, I’d like to thank all of you who have touched me in some way over this last year, all the thousands of you whom I’ve seen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to thank the computer executives and the electronics executives in Silicon Valley, two-thirds of whom are Republicans who said they wanted to sign on to a change in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to thank the hundreds of executives who came to Chicago, a third of them Republicans, who said they wanted to change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to thank the people who’ve started with Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Perot who’ve come on to help our campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to thank all the folks around America that no one ever knows about — the woman that was holding the AIDS baby she adopted in Cedar Rapids, Iowa who asked me to do something more for adoption; the woman who stopped along the road in Wisconsin and wept because her husband had lost his job after 27 years; all the people who are having a tough time and the people who are winning but who know how desperately we need to change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This debate tonight has made crystal clear a challenge that is as old as America — the choice between hope and fear, change or more of the same, the courage to move into a new tomorrow or to listen to the crowd who says things could be worse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Bush has said some very compelling things tonight that don’t quite square with the record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He was president for 3 years before he proposed a health care plan that still hasn’t been sent to Congress in total; three years before an economic plan, and he still didn’t say tonight that that tax bill he vetoed raised taxes only on the rich and gave the rest of you a break — but he vetoed it anyway.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I offer a new direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Invest in American jobs, American education, control health care costs, bring this country together again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want the future of this country to be as bright and brilliant as its past, and it can be if we have the courage to change.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you a little what it’s like to be president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In the Oval Office, you can’t predict what kind of crisis is going to come up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You have to make tough calls.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t be on one hand this way and one hand another.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t take different positions on these difficult issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then you need a philosophical — I’d call it a philosophical underpinning.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Mine for foreign affairs is democracy and freedom, and look at the dramatic changes around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Cold War is over.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Soviet Union is no more and we’re working with a democratic country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, the Baltics are free.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Take a look at the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We had to stand up against a tyrant.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The US came together as we haven’t in many, many years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we kicked this man out of Kuwait.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And in the process, as a result of that will and that decision and that toughness, we now have ancient enemies talking peace in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Nobody would have dreamed it possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think the biggest dividend of making these tough calls is the fact that we are less afraid of nuclear war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Every parent out there has much less worry that their kids are going to be faced with nuclear holocaust.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: All this is good.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: On the domestic side, what we must do is have change that empowers people — not change for the sake of change, tax and spend.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We don’t need to do that any more.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What we need to do is empower people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to invest and save.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to do better in education.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to do better in job retraining.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to expand our exports, and they’re going very, very well, indeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we need to strengthen the American family.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hope as president that I’ve earned your trust.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve admitted it when I make a mistake, but then I go on and help, try to solve the problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hope I’ve earned your trust because a lot of being president is about trust and character.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I ask for your support for 4 more years to finish this job.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very, very much.
